The '''2020 [[United States Olympic Trials (track and field)|United States Olympic trials for track and field]]''' were staged in [[Eugene, Oregon]], having been moved from the initially selected [[Hilmer Lodge Stadium]] in [[Walnut, California]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.sgvtribune.com/2018/05/01/mt-sac-loses-2020-olympic-track-and-field-trials/|title=Mt. SAC loses 2020 Olympic Track and Field trials|publisher=San Gabriel Valley Tribune|access-date=2018-06-25|archive-date=2018-06-25|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180625050555/https://www.sgvtribune.com/2018/05/01/mt-sac-loses-2020-olympic-track-and-field-trials/|url-status=live}}</ref> This was first major event for the redesigned and rebuilt [[Hayward Field]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.si.com/olympics/2018/08/02/eugene-2020-us-olympic-track-and-field-trials-hayward-field-renovation|title=2020 U.S. Olympic Track and Field trials return to Eugene|work=SI.com|access-date=2018-08-03|language=en|archive-date=2018-08-02|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180802202600/https://www.si.com/olympics/2018/08/02/eugene-2020-us-olympic-track-and-field-trials-hayward-field-renovation|url-status=live}}</ref>

Organized by [[USA Track and Field]] and [[TrackTown USA]], the ten-day competition was originally scheduled for June 19–28, 2020, but was rescheduled to June 18–27, 2021 due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States|COVID-19 pandemic]] and the postponement of the [[2020 Summer Olympics]] to 2021. It is serving as the [[national championships]] in [[track and field]] for the [[United States]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.latimes.com/sports/olympics/la-sp-olympic-team-trials-20170628-story.html |title=Mt. SAC will host 2020 U.S. Olympic track and field trials |newspaper=[[Los Angeles Times]] |date=June 28, 2017 |access-date=August 25, 2017 |author=Elliott, Helene |archive-date=August 25, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170825193447/http://www.latimes.com/sports/olympics/la-sp-olympic-team-trials-20170628-story.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.usatf.org/News/2020-U-S--Olympic-Team-Trials---Track---Field-awar.aspx |title=2020 U.S. Olympic Team trials – Track & Field awarded to Mt. SAC and L.A. area |publisher=[[USATF]] |date=June 28, 2017 |access-date=August 25, 2017 |author=Geer, Jill |archive-date=July 3, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170703215627/http://www.usatf.org/News/2020-U-S--Olympic-Team-Trials---Track---Field-awar.aspx |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine |url=https://www.si.com/olympics/2017/06/28/2020-us-olympic-trials-track-and-field-mt-sac-host-city-announced |title=2020 U.S. Olympic trials to be held at Mt. San Antonio College |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |date=June 28, 2017 |access-date=August 25, 2017 |author=CHAVEZ, CHRIS |archive-date=August 25, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170825190010/https://www.si.com/olympics/2017/06/28/2020-us-olympic-trials-track-and-field-mt-sac-host-city-announced |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.foxsports.com/olympics/story/2020-us-olympic-trials-track-and-field-mt-sac-host-city-announced-062817 |title=2020 U.S. Olympic trials to be held at Mt. San Antonio College |publisher=[[Fox Sports Networks]] |date=June 28, 2017 |access-date=August 25, 2017 |author=CHAVEZ, CHRIS |archive-date=August 25, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170825185337/http://www.foxsports.com/olympics/story/2020-us-olympic-trials-track-and-field-mt-sac-host-city-announced-062817 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.usatf.org/news/2020/new-dates-set-for-2020-u-s-olympic-team-trials-%e2%80%94-t|title=NEW DATES SET FOR 2020 U.S. OLYMPIC TEAM TRIALS — TRACK & FIELD|publisher=[[USA Track & Field]]|access-date=April 22, 2020|archive-date=April 22, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200422212244/https://www.usatf.org/news/2020/new-dates-set-for-2020-u-s-olympic-team-trials-%e2%80%94-t|url-status=live}}</ref>

The results of the event determined qualification for the [[United States at the 2020 Summer Olympics|American Olympic team]] at the 2020 Summer Olympics, to be held in [[Tokyo]]. Provided they had achieved the [[Athletics at the 2020 Summer Olympics – Qualification|Olympic standard]] or are in the [[World Athletics]] ranking quota, the top three athletes in each event gained a place on the Olympic team. In the event that a leading athlete did not hold the standard, or an athlete withdrew, the next highest finishing athlete with the standard was selected instead. USA Track and Field announced their Olympic roster based on these guidelines on July 6, 2021.<ref name=roster>{{Cite web|url=https://usatf.org/news/2021/team-usatf-announces-roster-for-2020-tokyo-olympic|title=USA Track & Field &#124; Team USATF announces roster for 2020 Tokyo Olympic Games|website=usatf.org|access-date=2021-10-06|archive-date=2021-08-18|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210818160420/https://www.usatf.org/news/2021/team-usatf-announces-roster-for-2020-tokyo-olympic|url-status=live}}</ref>

The [[2020 USA Marathon Championships|trials]] for the men's and women's marathon were held on February 29, 2020 in Atlanta<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://usatf.org/events/2020/2020-u-s-olympic-team-trials-marathon|title=USA Track & Field &#124; 2020 U.S. Olympic Team trials - Marathon|website=usatf.org|access-date=2021-10-06|archive-date=2021-05-31|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210531060854/https://www.usatf.org/events/2020/2020-u-s-olympic-team-trials-marathon|url-status=live}}</ref> and the trials for the men's 50&nbsp;km race walk were held on January 25, 2020 at [[San Diego Christian College]] and the [[Santee Town Center station]] in [[Santee, California]].

Multiple rising high school and collegiate track athletes such as Nico Young, [[Erriyon Knighton]], Hobbs Kessler, and [[Sha'Carri Richardson]] participated in the trials. Multiple world-leads, [[List of United States records in track and field|US records]], and [[List of world records in athletics|world records]] were broken during the trials such as [[Sydney McLaughlin]]'s 400m hurdles WR of 51.90 during the finals, [[Erriyon Knighton|Erriyon Knighton's]] U-18 and U-20 200m record of 19.84 in the finals, and [[Ryan Crouser|Ryan Crouser's]] shot put WR of 23.37m.

====Notes====
:{{note label|a|a|a}} [[Sha'Carri Richardson]] originally finished first in a time of 10.86, but she was suspended by [[World Athletics]] after testing positive for [[THC]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Pells |first1=Eddie |last2=Graham |first2=Pat |url=https://apnews.com/article/richardson-marijuana-test-olympic-100-5980fa868b14b54d4686591b01c65e46 |title=Richardson will miss Olympic 100 after marijuana test |work=[[Associated Press]] |date=2021-07-02 |access-date=2021-07-06 |archive-date=2021-07-03 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210703013146/https://apnews.com/article/richardson-marijuana-test-olympic-100-5980fa868b14b54d4686591b01c65e46 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Sha'Carri RICHARDSON |url=https://worldathletics.org/athletes/-/14717691 |website=World Athletics |access-date=22 June 2024}}</ref>
:{{note label|b|b|b}} [[Brianna McNeal]] originally finished second in a time of 12.51, but she was suspended for five years for an anti-doping rule violation (missed tests). While she was allowed to compete at the trials pending appeal, her suspension was later upheld.<ref>{{cite news |title=CAS upholds McNeal's five-year ban, hurdles champ to miss Tokyo Olympics |url=https://www.reuters.com/lifestyle/sports/cas-upholds-mcneals-five-year-ban-hurdles-champ-miss-tokyo-olympics-2021-07-02/ |work=Reuters |date=2 July 2021 |access-date=2021-07-06 |archive-date=2021-07-11 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210711082258/https://www.reuters.com/lifestyle/sports/cas-upholds-mcneals-five-year-ban-hurdles-champ-miss-tokyo-olympics-2021-07-02/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Brianna MCNEAL |url=https://worldathletics.org/athletes/_/14320208 |website=World Athletics |access-date=22 June 2024}}</ref>
:{{note label|c|c|c}} Neither McPherson nor Greene achieved the Olympic standard or a qualifying world ranking. In addition to Cunningham, USATF selected fourth-placed [[Rachel McCoy]] who previously achieved the Olympic standard, and [[Tynita Butts]], who did not reach the finals but held a qualifying ranking of #21.<ref name=roster/>
:{{note label|d|d|d}} Hazlewood had not achieved the Olympic standard or a qualifying world ranking. Fourth place [[Kelsey Card]], who had a qualifying ranking of #23, was instead selected.<ref name=roster/>
:{{note label|e|e|e}} Allgood-Whetstone had not achieved the Olympic standard or a qualifying world ranking. Fourth place [[Ariana Ince]], who had a qualifying ranking of #16, was instead selected.<ref name=roster/>

==Qualification==
USA Track & Field sets minimum performances standards for entry into the national championships. In order to merit entry into the championships, an athlete must meet that standard, or better, within a set time frame prior to the competition.

All qualifying performances for the U.S. Olympic trials must be attained on a '''standard outdoor track''' in the period
* Wednesday, May 1, 2019 through Sunday, June 6, 2021,

or on an '''indoor track''', in the same event, in the period 
* Wednesday, January 1, 2020 through Sunday, June 6, 2021;

except for the 10,000 meters, Decathlon & Heptathlon and 20&nbsp;km Race Walks, whose qualifying period is from 
* Tuesday, January 1, 2019 through Sunday, June 6, 2021.

The qualifying performance for the men's 50&nbsp;km Race walk must be attained in the period 
* Monday January 1, 2018 through Sunday, January 12, 2020.
<ref name=QS>[http://www.usatf.org/Events---Calendar/2020/U-S--Olympic-Team-Trials---Track---Field/Athlete-Information/Qualifying-Standards.aspx 2020 USATF Olympic trials Qualifying Standards] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191108131216/http://www.usatf.org/Events---Calendar/2020/U-S--Olympic-Team-Trials---Track---Field/Athlete-Information/Qualifying-Standards.aspx |date=2019-11-08 }} [[USATF]]</ref>

There are also automatic qualifying criteria outside of the entry standards. Athletes who are the reigning indoor or outdoor national champion are automatically qualified to enter that event.

Qualifying marks must be attained in a 2020 U.S. Olympic trials event. No qualifying marks will be allowed using alternate events, except for the men's Mile run as follows: An appeal to use a Mile qualifying mark for the 1500 will be accepted only if the mile mark was made during the 2020 season, from Wednesday, January 1, 2020 through Sunday, June 6, 2021, and the mark is 3:54.00 or better.<ref>[http://www.usatf.org/usatf/files/da/daf2d12d-b51c-475c-9b06-4a6b41d81071.pdf USATF 2019 Competition Rules] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190729214943/http://www.usatf.org/usatf/files/da/daf2d12d-b51c-475c-9b06-4a6b41d81071.pdf |date=2019-07-29 }}. USATF. Retrieved 2019-07-29.</ref>

For events over distances from 100&nbsp;m to 800&nbsp;m, performances will only be accepted if [[fully automatic timing]] (FAT) is used. For performances beyond that distance, FAT times are also used, but in the event that the athlete has not recorded a FAT performance, a manually recorded time may be used. There will be no adjustment for marks made at altitude. Wind-assisted performances will not be accepted for 2020 U.S. Olympic trials qualifying.
